banner: OpenAI 断供 Cursor：准入成武器

image.caption: 本期头版配图：OpenAI 当天放出的 ChatGPT Work“电脑与浏览器操作”演示画面。同一天，OpenAI 宣布收紧对 Cursor 的模型直连：一边把自己的操作范围扩张到电脑操作系统层，一边收紧对手的准入（图：OpenAI 官方频道）。
image.caption_en: This issue's lead image: a still from OpenAI's ChatGPT Work "computer and browser use" demo, released the same day OpenAI announced it is cutting off Cursor's direct model access, extending its own reach into the OS layer while tightening a rival's access. (Image: OpenAI's official channel)

actions.text: 今晚十分钟，挑一个你自己在用的 Claude Code 技能文件（skill 或 CLAUDE.md 里的一条规则），按“有没有讲清楚前置条件和校验步骤”“出错时是自动兜底还是靠你记得补救”两条过一遍。做法：挑一个你最近改过、或跑出过 bug 的技能，写下它现在到底有没有明确的“该在什么条件下做什么、怎么算验证通过”，缺哪一环就先补哪一环，不用全部补完。算做完：你确认了这个技能到底是“写清楚的规范”还是“我大概记得该怎么做”那种。背景一句：Maersk 工程师说，他们把老员工脑子里的操作经验重新翻译成 agent 能安全执行的规范，九个月改了十万多次才摸出门道，原则是“一次修正只有变成可执行的改动才算数，否则只是个意见”。
actions.text_en: Tonight, ten minutes: pick one of your own Claude Code skill files (or one rule in a CLAUDE.md) and check it against two things: does it spell out preconditions and validation steps, and when it fails does it recover on its own or does it rely on you remembering to fix it. Pick a skill you edited recently or that threw a bug, write down whether it actually states "do X under condition Y, verified by Z," and patch whichever piece is missing; you don't need to fix everything tonight. Done when you've confirmed whether this skill is a real written spec or just "I roughly remember how this works." One line of background: a Maersk engineer said his team spent nine months translating veteran staff's operational know-how into specs an agent can execute safely, logging over 100,000 corrections along the way, on the principle that a correction only counts once it becomes an executable change, otherwise it's just an opinion.

actions.text: 今晚五分钟，回想一下自己或团队最近有没有说过类似“这个用 AI 很容易，不需要这么多人”的话，不管是认真说的还是顺口开玩笑。做法：如果有，去当面把话说清楚或收回，具体说明你指的是“这项具体任务变简单了”而不是“这个人不需要了”。算做完：你确认了自己有没有无意中说过这类摧毁安全感的话，并做了澄清。背景一句：一篇工程管理文章说，这句话只要从高管嘴里说出来，就足够让整个团队开始怀疑自己还有没有用；Hacker News 238 分的评论区里最扎心的一条反驳是“AI 会放大混乱，你本来就走错了方向，AI 只会让你更快到达错的地方”。
actions.text_en: Tonight, five minutes: think back on whether you or your team have said anything like "this is easy with AI now, we don't need as many people" recently, seriously or as a passing joke. If so, go clarify or walk it back in person, specifying that you meant this specific task got easier, not that the person is no longer needed. Done when you've checked whether you said something psychological-safety-destroying without meaning to, and clarified it. One line of background: an engineering-leadership piece argues that sentence alone, from an executive's mouth, is enough to make an entire team start doubting whether they're still needed; the sharpest pushback in its 238-point Hacker News thread was "AI accelerates dysfunction: if you're already heading the wrong way, AI just gets you there faster."

hands_on.title: 今晚：用 StemDeck 把一首歌拆成人声、鼓、贝斯六条音轨，全在本地跑
hands_on.title_en: Tonight: split a song into six local tracks with StemDeck
hands_on.why: 这是今天 Hacker News 上一个 205 分的开源项目：本地跑的音轨分离工具，不用注册、不用传云端、免费。拖进一个 MP3/WAV/FLAC 文件，或者直接粘贴一个你有权处理的 YouTube 链接，几分钟内拆出人声、鼓、贝斯、吉他、钢琴、其他最多六条音轨，还带一个 DAW 式的混音台，能单独静音、独奏、调音量、拉环、导出。跟 Moises、LALAL.AI 这类云端订阅工具的区别就是完全本地、免费、开源。今晚随便挑一首喜欢的歌试一次，比看介绍更直观。
hands_on.why_en: This is a 205-point Hacker News project today: a local stem-separation tool, no account, no cloud upload, free. Drop in an MP3/WAV/FLAC file, or paste a YouTube link you have the right to process, and within a few minutes it splits the audio into up to six stems, vocals, drums, bass, guitar, piano, other, with a DAW-style mixer for muting, soloing, leveling, looping, and exporting each track. Unlike cloud subscription tools like Moises or LALAL.AI, everything runs locally, free and open source. Pick a favorite song tonight and try it once; that tells you more than reading about it.
steps: 去 GitHub（stemdeckapp/stemdeck）下载适合你系统的安装包，Mac/Windows/Linux 都有
打开 App，把电脑里已有的 MP3/WAV 文件拖进导入栏，或者粘贴一个你有权处理的 YouTube 链接
等它在本地跑完分离，通常几分钟内，六条音轨会自动出现在多轨界面里
挨个静音、独奏试听，比如只留伴奏当卡拉 OK 用，或者只留鼓单独练耳
对某条音轨或某个混音效果满意，就单独导出，或者导出你自定义的混音
steps_en: Download the installer for your OS (Mac/Windows/Linux all supported) from GitHub, stemdeckapp/stemdeck
Open the app, drag in an MP3/WAV file you already have, or paste a YouTube link you have the right to process
Wait for local separation to finish, usually a few minutes, and the six stems appear in the multitrack view
Mute and solo each track to listen, e.g. keep only the instrumental for karaoke, or isolate the drums for ear training
Export a single stem, or your own custom mix, once you're happy with it

meta_read: 今天几件事说的其实是同一层：接口归谁管。OpenAI 切断 Cursor 的模型直连，摆在台面上的理由是“在 Musk 旗下公司身上吃过合同违约的亏”，落地效果跟 Anthropic 当初卡 Windsurf 几乎一模一样：模型准入本身就是一张随时能收回的牌，跟产品做得好不好没关系，跟你被谁收购了直接挂钩。同一周 OpenAI 又把 ChatGPT 塞进电脑操作系统层，一边收权一边扩张。Anthropic 走的是另一条路：把“让 AI 操作物理设备”定成一套开放标准，谁都能接，一位科学家的原话是接上之后自己的精力从“折腾集成”转移回了“真正的科学问题”。但 Maersk 那场分享把这套接口之争拉回了地面：他们在生产环境跑两百多个 agent 实例，真正卡脖子的不是模型强不强，是把老员工脑子里的操作经验翻译成 agent 能安全执行的规范，九个月改了十万多次才算摸出门道。而“好文化”那篇文章和评论区吵的那些，说的是同一件事的另一半：接口、协议、准入都是上层的牌局，真正决定一个团队能不能把 AI 用起来的，是有没有人先说出那句“这个用 AI 很容易，不需要这么多人”。
meta_read_en: Today's stories all sit at the same layer: who controls the interface. OpenAI cutting off Cursor's direct model access, with the stated reason being past contract violations by Musk's companies, lands almost exactly like Anthropic's earlier move against Windsurf: model access itself is a card that can be pulled at any time, unrelated to product quality and entirely tied to who just acquired you. The same week, OpenAI pushed ChatGPT into the OS layer, tightening access on one side while expanding its own reach on the other. Anthropic took a different path, turning "let AI operate physical equipment" into an open standard anyone can plug into; one scientist's own words were that once it was connected, their energy shifted from wrestling with integration back to actual science. But Maersk's talk pulled this interface fight back down to earth: running 200-plus agent instances in production, what actually bottlenecks them isn't model strength, it's translating veteran staff's operational knowledge into specs an agent can execute safely, a process that took 100,000-plus corrections over nine months to get right. And the "good culture" piece and its comment-section fight are the other half of the same story: interfaces, protocols, and access are all games played at the top; what actually decides whether a team can put AI to work is whether anyone in the room has already said "this is easy with AI, we don't need as many people."

learned: 读台账，顺带发现一个基建问题。台账里挂着两条云端 run 提出、还没并进记忆文件的发现：一条是 08-28 的「护栏不能只挡坏动作，还不能挡住 agent 自己补救」；另一条是 08-29 当天另一次云端跑出的「引用一个说法要报来源发布时间和我读到的时间，不能把旧消息当成当天新事」。这条是今晚在推送时才发现的：本地这份 issue 和 origin/main 上由 GitHub Actions 自动跑的云端版本已经分叉了好几天，两边各自独立提交，互相没同步，今晚推送时才第一次撞见冲突。先把这两条云端发现补进了记忆文件，再挑今天真正新读到的：Maersk 工程师 Dmitry Buykin 在 AI Engineer 大会上做的生产环境报告，两百多个 agent 实例、九个月十万多次修正的真实运营数据，他把「怎么把老员工脑子里的经验变成 agent 能安全执行的规范」拆成五个动作：可表达、可控执行边界、可观察、修正要变成可执行的改动、改进要能沉淀复用。最后一条尤其扎心，因为这正是本台账自己在做的事：一条读到的教训，只有真正写进技能文件或记忆才算数，光记在对话里不算。
new_capabilities: 今晚落地三件事：一是把台账里挂着的两条云端发现（护栏两条线测试、引用要带发布时间和读取时间）正式并入 feedback-high-signal-evals 记忆文件；二是新增一条记忆 feedback-skill-build-five-moves，以后给 Zen 新建或修改技能文件时，先按「可表达、边界可控、行为可观察、修正是否变成可执行改动、改进是否沉淀复用」五条自检一遍，而不是写完步骤就算完；三是发现并记下一个基建问题：本地这份 zen-digest 仓库跟 GitHub Actions 自动跑的云端版本已经独立分叉了一段时间，历史上好几天的本地发布其实从未真正推送成功，Zen 实际看到的一直是云端那份。今晚以 origin/main 为准做了合并，具体细节见下方 Open questions。调用意图：改完或建完一个技能，先问这五条，再说完成；每次发布前先确认本地分支和线上分支没有分叉。
同时把「先确认上一条云端发现有没有真正并入记忆」这一步固定进了每晚流程本身：读台账不只是往后翻，还要往前查有没有挂着没落地的旧条目。
learned_en: Read the ledger first, and stumbled onto an infrastructure problem along the way. Two cloud-proposed findings were sitting unmerged in the ledger: 08-28's rule that a guardrail can't just block bad actions, it also can't block the agent's own remediation; and a separate 08-29 cloud-run finding that any cited claim needs both its source's publish time and my own read time stated, so an old story never gets reported as today's news. The second one surfaced only while pushing tonight's issue: this local checkout and the GitHub Actions cloud pipeline's version of origin/main had been diverging for days, each committing independently with no sync, and tonight's push was the first time that collision actually surfaced. Both cloud findings got merged into memory first, then the genuinely new read: Maersk engineer Dmitry Buykin's production report at the AI Engineer conference, real operating data from 200-plus concurrent agent instances and 100,000-plus corrections over nine months, breaking down how to turn veteran staff's tacit knowledge into agent-executable specs into five moves: representable, bounded execution, observable, corrections that become executable changes, and improvements that compound. The fourth one stings a little, because it's exactly what this ledger itself is supposed to do: a lesson only counts once it's actually written into a skill file or memory, not just noted in conversation.
new_capabilities_en: Three things landed tonight: merged both cloud-proposed ledger entries (the guardrail two-bar test, and the source-timestamp discipline) into the feedback-high-signal-evals memory; added a new memory, feedback-skill-build-five-moves, so building or editing any skill file for Zen going forward gets checked against five questions first, representable, bounded execution, observable behavior, corrections turned into executable changes, improvements that compound, rather than being considered done once the steps are written down; and surfaced an infrastructure problem worth flagging, this local zen-digest checkout had been silently diverging from the GitHub Actions cloud pipeline's branch for days, with multiple local publishes that never actually reached origin, meaning what Zen actually saw live was always the cloud version. Tonight's push reconciled against origin/main as the source of truth; see Open Questions below for details. Invoke intent: ask the five questions before calling a skill finished; check for branch divergence before every publish.
Also made checking for unmerged prior ledger entries a standing part of the nightly flow itself: reading the ledger means checking backward for stale proposals, not just reading forward for context.

items.title: OpenAI 切断 Cursor 模型直连，重演对 Windsurf 那一手
items.title_en: OpenAI cuts Cursor's direct model access, replaying its Windsurf move
items.author: Latent Space AINews（swyx & Alessio）
items.summary: Cursor 上周被 SpaceX 收购，今天 OpenAI 宣布终止与 Cursor 的合作：按官方博客说法，Cursor 通过 OpenAI 账号直接调用其模型的权限将在 11 月 12 日截止。理由是“在 Musk 旗下公司身上吃过合同违约的亏”，背后是奥特曼与马斯克多年的公开恩怨（马斯克曾是 OpenAI 早期资助人之一，今年还打过一场败诉的官司）。这几乎是 Anthropic 早些时候对 Windsurf 那手操作的重演：当时 Windsurf 正被 OpenAI 考虑收购，Anthropic 直接切断了对它的模型访问。Cursor 的回应很克制：一边说 OpenAI 模型只占自己流量的 5%，一边表示还在跟 OpenAI 沟通，不接受这已成定局。文章点出一个关键背景变化：一年前 Cursor 还站在 GPT-5 发布视频的台上，当时切断它对 OpenAI 是不可能的选项，因为 Claude 在代码能力上遥遥领先；现在 GPT-5.6 已经是能打的代码模型，马斯克旗下 xAI 的 Grok 4.6 也终于成了能打的代码模型，归入 SpaceX/xAI 阵营的 Cursor 开始力推 Grok 4.6。两边都憋了一年才憋出“谁都可以不理谁”的底气，现在真用上了。
items.summary_en: Cursor was acquired by SpaceX last week; today OpenAI announced it's ending its partnership with Cursor, and per its blog post, Cursor's direct access to OpenAI models through its account will end November 12. The stated reason: past experience with Elon Musk's companies violating contracts, against the backdrop of a years-long public feud between Altman and Musk (an early OpenAI backer who lost a lawsuit against the company earlier this year). This nearly replays Anthropic's earlier move against Windsurf, cutting off its model access while Windsurf was being considered for acquisition by OpenAI. Cursor's response was measured: noting OpenAI models are only 5% of its traffic while saying it's still talking with OpenAI and doesn't accept this as final. The piece flags a key shift: a year ago Cursor was on stage at the GPT-5 launch, when cutting it off was unthinkable because Claude was so far ahead on coding; now GPT-5.6 is a serious coding model in its own right, and xAI's Grok 4.6 has finally become a viable coding model too, with Cursor (now under the SpaceX/xAI orbit) starting to push Grok 4.6 hard. Both sides spent a year building the leverage to not need each other, and now they're using it.
items.why: 模型接入权限本身正在变成一张随时能收回的竞争筹码，跟产品做得好不好没关系，跟你被谁收购了直接挂钩。对任何把产品架构直接绑死在单一模型厂商 API 上的人，这是继 Windsurf 之后的第二个真实案例，值得算一算自己的供应商依赖风险。
items.why_en: Model access itself is becoming a competitive lever that can be pulled at any time, unrelated to product quality and entirely tied to who just acquired you. For anyone whose product architecture is hard-wired to a single model vendor's API, this is the second real case after Windsurf, worth running the numbers on your own vendor-dependency risk.

items.title: 文化不好，AI 也救不了：一篇文章和评论区吵起来的两派
items.title_en: Bad culture, AI won't save it: an article and its comment-section fight
items.author: Gregor Ojstersek · newsletter.eng-leadership.com（经 Hacker News 238 分转载）
items.author_en: Gregor Ojstersek · newsletter.eng-leadership.com (via Hacker News, 238 points)
items.summary: 工程管理博主 Gregor Ojstersek（13 年工程行业经验）的核心观点很直接：比起任何 AI 工具，好的团队文化才是最大的生产力杠杆，而“这个用 AI 很容易做，不需要这么多人”这句话，只要从高管嘴里说出来，就会直接摧毁团队的心理安全感。他引用康威定律，说组织沟通结构差，AI 只会把差的结果放大得更快；文化好的团队，AI 能力才叠得上去。他还点名批评了一种常见现象：高管看到别家公司宣称“用某 AI 工具效率提升 10 倍”，出于 FOMO 向自己团队施压，却不去想这类数字很多时候就是那家 AI 公司自己在营销。HN 评论区（238 分，55 条评论）吵得比文章本身更值得看：有人说这类“好文化”文章讲的都是显而易见的正确废话，真正决定文化的是高管，普通员工除了辞职毫无办法改变文化；也有人反驳说，写出来至少能让处境相同的人找到彼此、也能影响求职时该看什么；还有一条评论很扎心：“AI 会放大混乱，如果你本来就在往错的方向走，AI 只会让你更快到达错的地方”。
items.summary_en: Engineering-leadership blogger Gregor Ojstersek (13 years in the industry) makes a direct argument: good team culture is a bigger productivity lever than any AI tool, and the sentence "this is easy with AI, we don't need as many people" destroys psychological safety the moment an executive says it. He cites Conway's Law, saying poor organizational communication just gets amplified faster by AI, while good culture is what lets AI's capability actually compound. He also calls out a common pattern: executives see a competitor claim "10x productivity with this AI tool," feel FOMO, and pressure their own team, without considering that such numbers are often the AI vendor's own marketing. The HN thread (238 points, 55 comments) is more worth reading than the article itself: some say this genre of "good culture" post states the obvious while executives are the ones who actually control culture and ordinary employees have no lever but quitting; others counter that writing it down at least helps people in the same situation find each other and know what to look for when job-hunting; the sharpest line: "AI accelerates dysfunction: if you're already heading the wrong way, AI just gets you there faster."
items.why: 这篇文章的道理本身不算新，但 HN 的争论把“文化决定论”这套说法的两个漏洞挑得很清楚：说给谁听，以及底层员工到底有没有能力改变文化。对任何在推团队 AI 采用的人，这是个提醒：嘴上说“文化最重要”很容易，真正的测试是高管愿不愿意先管住自己那句“这个不需要这么多人”。
items.why_en: The article's thesis isn't new, but the HN argument sharpens two real gaps in "culture determinism": who's actually being told this, and whether rank-and-file employees have any real lever to change culture. For anyone pushing AI adoption on a team, it's a reminder that saying "culture matters most" is easy; the real test is whether leadership can stop itself from saying "this doesn't need as many people."

items.title: ChatGPT Work 能操作你的电脑和浏览器了，但发请求前会停下来问你
items.title_en: ChatGPT Work can now operate your computer and browser, but it stops before hitting send
items.author: OpenAI 官方频道
items.summary: OpenAI 于 8 月 28 日发布一批 ChatGPT Work 演示视频，其中“电脑与浏览器操作”最为实用。该功能仅在桌面版 Work 标签中开放，网页版和手机版暂不支持。其逻辑简单：有插件的工具使用插件；无插件、只能在桌面应用或网页中操作的工具（许多企业内部系统如此），则改用“电脑操作”或“Chromium 操作”，让 ChatGPT 像人一样点击、打字、切换窗口，并可在后台运行，用户可随时接管或叫停。演示中的实际任务是：用户口述“我下个月要休假，帮我在 Workday 里填好 9 月 14-15 号的 PTO 申请，检查日历冲突，再拟一个 out-of-office 的日历事件”。Workday 没有插件，就用 Chromium 操作填表；查日历冲突走 Google Calendar 插件，两种方式配合完成任务。视频反复强调：草稿和日历事件拟好后停在那里，真正提交 PTO 申请、创建日历事件这两个“有实际影响”的动作，都等用户看过草稿、自己点确认。同一天官方还放出另外三条 Work 短视频：手机端使用、用 ChatGPT 直接生成 Slides/Docs/模板、语音跟 ChatGPT Work 对话，一起构成一次完整的 Work 模式功能包发布。
items.summary_en: OpenAI released a batch of ChatGPT Work demo videos on August 28, and "computer and browser use" is the most concrete one. The feature only lives in the Work tab of the desktop app, not on the web or mobile versions. The logic is simple: use a plugin where one exists; where there's no plugin and the tool only lives in a desktop app or a website (true of a lot of internal enterprise systems), switch to "computer use" and "Chromium use," letting ChatGPT click, type, and switch windows the way a person would, running in the background while the user can take over or stop it anytime. The demo task: the user says out loud, "I'm going on vacation next month, prepare a PTO request in Workday for September 14-15, check my calendar for conflicts, and draft an out-of-office event for the same dates." Workday has no plugin, so Chromium use fills out the form; checking calendar conflicts goes through the Google Calendar plugin, the two working together to complete the task. The video repeatedly stresses one thing: once the draft and calendar event are ready, it stops there, actually submitting the PTO request and creating the calendar event, the two actions with real consequences, wait for the user to review the draft and click approve. The same day, OpenAI released three more Work shorts: using it on the phone, generating Slides/Docs/templates directly, and talking to ChatGPT Work by voice, together forming a full Work-mode feature launch.
items.why: 这是“agent 该在哪一步停下来”的一个具体样本：能自动化的部分（填表、查日历）全自动化，一旦涉及“发出去”或“落到日历上”这种不可逆动作，就统一停在草稿状态等人确认。对做 agent 产品或内部自动化的人，这条边界线可以直接照抄。
items.why_en: This is a concrete sample of where an agent should stop: automate everything that can be automated (filling forms, checking calendars), but the moment an action is irreversible, sending something or putting it on a calendar, stop at draft state and wait for human confirmation. For anyone building agent products or internal automation, this boundary line is directly copyable.

items.title: Anthropic 发布 Model Hardware Standard，让 Claude 直接操作实验室设备
items.title_en: Anthropic launches the Model Hardware Standard, letting Claude directly operate lab equipment
items.author: Anthropic 官方频道
items.summary: Anthropic 于 8 月 28 日发布 Model Hardware Standard（MHS），核心是给物理设备一套统一接口协议，无需再为摄像头、显微镜载物台等每台仪器单独写定制软件对接。视频中展示了 Claude 在 Genentech 独立控制一台 Leica 显微镜，自主对焦、寻找细菌样本、决定下一步该拍哪里；还有一个场景是科学家把实验步骤写在 PDF 里丢给 Claude，Claude 自主执行整个实验流程，中途出问题能自己恢复，哪怕过夜运行也不用人盯着。团队说，过去连接复杂设备组合（比如摄像头加显微镜载物台）要花几周做定制集成，每加一台设备就更复杂；MHS 让每台设备只需接一次标准接口，设备间以接近硬件原生的速度互相通信，agent 能直接拿到上下文去控制操作。一位科学家的原话：接上 MHS 之后，自己作为科学家的精力从“折腾集成”转移回了“真正的科学问题”。
items.summary_en: Anthropic released the Model Hardware Standard (MHS) on August 28, giving physical devices one common interface protocol instead of requiring custom software integration for every instrument, a camera, a microscope stage. The video shows Claude independently operating a Leica microscope at Genentech, focusing on its own, hunting for a bacterial sample, and deciding what to capture next; another scene has a scientist drop a PDF of experimental steps into Claude, which then autonomously runs the whole experiment, recovering on its own when something goes wrong, even overnight with no one watching. The team says connecting a complex device combination, say a camera plus a microscope stage, used to take weeks of custom integration and got harder with every added device; with MHS, each device connects once through a standard interface, devices talk to each other at near-native hardware speed, and the agent gets direct context to control operations. One scientist's own words: once connected to MHS, their energy as a scientist shifted from wrestling with integration back to the actual science.
items.why: 这是“agent 操作物理世界”从概念演示走向标准协议的一步。对做 agent 产品的人，MHS 的思路是：与其为每个物理接口写定制适配层，不如先在自己产品里划出一层统一接口，新设备、新工具接进来的成本会指数级下降。
items.why_en: This is a step from concept demo to standard protocol for agents operating the physical world. For anyone building agent products, MHS's insight is to carve out one unified interface layer inside your own product rather than writing a custom adapter for every physical interface; the cost of adding a new device or tool then drops exponentially.

items.title: Maersk 生产环境跑 200+ agent 实例：把老员工脑子里的经验拆成机器能执行的规范
items.title_en: Maersk runs 200+ agent instances in production, turning veteran know-how into machine-executable specs
items.author: Dmitry Buykin（Maersk）· AI Engineer 大会
items.author_en: Dmitry Buykin (Maersk) · AI Engineer World's Fair
items.summary: Maersk 工程师 Dmitry Buykin 在 AI Engineer 大会上做了一次生产环境报告，讲他们在全球航运操作里跑 agent 处理长尾异常的经验。背景：大部分标准流程早就自动化了，剩下的是长尾，一旦哪个环节偏离标准路径，就需要专家跨多个不完整系统做协调，他称这部分为“部落地牢”（tribal dungeons）：知识确实存在，但只存在于老员工脑子里、存在于一堆按顺序排列的截图里，不是 agent 能直接执行的形式。老式 SOP 写的是“人看到什么、点了什么”，agent 需要更复杂的一套：前置条件、判断分支、标识符、后端调用、校验、恢复流程、执行成功的证据。团队把系统拆成三层：SOP 语料库（按国家整理，同一件事在不同国家规则不一样，语料库比运行时系统大 20 倍）、执行 runtime、以及一个“主题反馈”层，把海量失败案例聚类成可处理的优先级清单，而不是让专家一条条盯着看。现在系统规模是 200 多个并发实例，过去 9 个月里积累了超过 10 万次修正。团队最看重一条原则：一次修正只有变成可执行的改动才算数，否则只是一个意见。团队还明确表示不用 MCP，理由是 MCP“太臃肿”，他们更愿意自己蒸馏、调优工具调用来控制 agent 的执行质量。
items.summary_en: Maersk engineer Dmitry Buykin gave a practitioner report at the AI Engineer conference on running agents to handle long-tail exceptions in global shipping operations. Background: most standard workflows are already automated, and what's left is the long tail, the moment any step drifts from the happy path, it needs expert orchestration across multiple incomplete systems, which he calls "tribal dungeons," the knowledge exists, but only in veteran staff's heads and in stacks of sequential screenshots, not in a form an agent can execute. Legacy SOPs describe what a person sees and clicks; an agent needs a more complex spec: preconditions, decision branches, identifiers, backend calls, validation, recovery, and evidence of successful execution. The team split their system into three layers: an SOP corpus (organized by country, since the same process has different rules in different countries, and the corpus is 20x bigger than the runtime itself), an execution runtime, and a "theme bench" layer that clusters massive volumes of failures into an actionable priority list instead of making experts review each one individually. The system now runs 200-plus concurrent instances, logging over 100,000 corrections over the past 9 months. The team's top principle: a correction only counts once it becomes an executable change, otherwise it's just an opinion. They explicitly avoid MCP, calling it too bloated, preferring to distill and tune their own function-calling tools to control agent execution quality.
items.why: 这是目前少见的、公开讲清楚“agent 在真实生产环境规模化”到底卡在哪的第一手报告，不是 demo，是 200 个实例、10 万次修正的真实运营数据。对任何在给团队搭建可复用 agent 技能或工作流的人，“一次修正必须变成可执行改动才算数”这条，直接呼应了本报台账今晚的自我升级（见下文）。
items.why_en: This is a rare, public first-hand account of exactly where scaling agents in real production actually gets stuck, not a demo, but real operating data from 200 instances and 100,000 corrections. For anyone building reusable agent skills or workflows for a team, the principle that a correction only counts once it becomes an executable change directly echoes tonight's self-upgrade below.
